rationale:
Issue #117 reports that expected headers are ignored when absent from actual requests due to iterating over actual.keys instead of expected.keys in map matching logic. The 4-line production patch swaps the iteration target from actual.keys to expected.keys and inverts the containment check, ensuring all expected map entries are validated. The trigger test 'fails on unsatisfied header expectation' sets a header expectation (contentLengthHeader: Matchers.integer) that is absent from the actual request and verifies an AssertionError is thrown. Runtime evidence confirms: buggy_differential shows this test fails deterministically on buggy revision (reproduced), passes on fixed revision (fixed_clean), full_suite.buggy_reproduces_only_triggers confirms no spurious failures, and all matrix runs (32 total, 3 repetitions per fingerprint) passed validation gates. The minimized production patch is identical to production-fix.patch and contains only the logic correction with no refactoring, formatting, or unrelated changes. No active duplicates in same project.

Issue #117 identifies that expected headers are ignored because the code iterates over actual.keys instead of expected.keys at line 75 of matches_request.dart. The minimized production patch fixes exactly this by swapping the iteration from `actual.keys.toList()` to `expected.keys.toList()` and inverting the containment check from `!expected.containsKey(key)` to `!actual.containsKey(key)`. This is a pure logic fix with no refactoring, formatting, or feature extension. The trigger test 'fails on unsatisfied header expectation' validates the fix by setting a header expectation (Headers.contentLengthHeader: Matchers.integer) that is absent from the actual request, expecting an AssertionError to be thrown. Runtime evidence confirms: buggy version fails the trigger test (silently ignores missing expected header), fixed version passes (throws AssertionError as expected), both versions build successfully, full suite passes on fixed, and the trigger is deterministic across 3 repetitions. The trigger test is the upstream test from the fixing commit with no modifications or new production APIs. No active duplicate root causes exist in this project.
